claim.pdf_says: 14.9.13.4   General rules  (bold run-in heading, one level below '14.9.13 EVALUATE statement', same level as 14.9.13.1 General and 14.9.13.2 General format)
claim.markdown_says: ## 14.9.13.4 General rules   (H2 -- while '### 14.9.13.1 General' and '### 14.9.13.2 General format' are H3 and the parent is '## 14.9.13 EVALUATE statement')
claim.why_it_matters: Same defect: the EVALUATE general rules become a sibling of the EVALUATE statement rather than a child, breaking the outline. (14.9.13.3 Syntax rules, on page 650, is H2 for the same reason.)

verdict.reasoning: Both sides of the claim were independently verified and both quotations are exact. PDF page 651 (printed folio 621) opens with the bold run-in heading whose glyphs I read directly as '14.9.13.4   General rules', followed by general rules 1) through 4). By ISO's own clause numbering a four-component number is subordinate to the three-component 14.9.13, and the typography confirms it: page 649 prints '14.9.13.3   Syntax rules' in the identical bold, identical-size run-in style, so .3 and .4 are peers one level under 14.9.13. On the markdown side, specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 26939 is literally '## 14.9.13.4 General rules' (H2), while line 26811 is '## 14.9.13 EVALUATE statement' (H2, the parent), and lines 26814/26819 are '### 14.9.13.1 General' and '### 14.9.13.2 General format' (H3). The heading therefore sits at the same depth as its own parent and one level above its own siblings, inverting the hierarchy. I checked that this is a defect and not a deliberate transcription convention: the dominant encoding for four-component clause numbers is H3 (620 occurrences) against 162 at H2 and 24 at H4, and neighbouring statement clauses transcribed correctly -- 14.9.9.1-.4, 14.9.15.1-.4 and 14.9.16.1-.4 -- are uniformly H3 for all four subclauses. Within 14.9 the H2 instances are scattered and internally inconsistent (14.9.12.3 is H3 but 14.9.14.3 is H2), which is the signature of transcription noise rather than a rule. This is not mere formatting: heading depth is the only machine-readable encoding of clause hierarchy in the markdown, so any consumer that slices the document by heading depth terminates the '14.9.13 EVALUATE statement' section before its Syntax rules and General rules, silently dropping the normative rules that govern the statement. No rejection ground applies -- the text is not reflowed away, the difference is not page-break furniture, wrapping or hyphenation, and neither source is misquoted.
verdict.corrected_description: Real defect, but the kind label 'missing-heading' is inaccurate: nothing is missing. The heading is present on page 651 with the correct number and the correct title, verbatim. The defect is heading DEPTH -- specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 26939 emits '## 14.9.13.4 General rules' at H2, making it a sibling of its own parent '## 14.9.13 EVALUATE statement' (line 26811) and one level shallower than its own siblings '### 14.9.13.1 General' (26814) and '### 14.9.13.2 General format' (26819). Correct depth is H3. The right kind is 'heading-level' / 'outline-depth', severity structural. Two further corrections to the claim: (a) the parenthetical misplaces the companion defect -- 14.9.13.3 Syntax rules is on page 649 (printed folio 619), inside the markdown's '## Page 649' block at line 26868, not page 650; page 650 carries only syntax rules 7)-10) and Table 15. (b) This is not a page-651 one-off but one instance of a document-wide class: 162 four-component clause headings are emitted at H2 against 620 correctly at H3, so the ledger should record it as a systemic pattern to be swept in one pass, not repaired page by page.
